items.label: Budget Uncertainty Reserve
items.note: Offsets revenue and spending risk in the forecast

context.text: A 2022 State tax-agency error overpaid Fremont about $20 million in tax revenue; the City is paying it back from reserves.
In FY 2024/25 the City applied $19.9 million from its Budget Uncertainty Reserve to cover the one-time sales tax shortfall.
The FY 2026/27 Proposed Budget says there is no capacity to restore eliminated positions or services.
The City reports 0.9 sworn police officers per 1,000 residents, compared with a California average of 2.
Fremont has a population of 232,619 across 92 square miles.

timeline.title: FY 2025/26 budget adopted
timeline.text: A $392.4 million Operating Budget, balanced without the Budget Uncertainty Reserve. Infrastructure maintenance is reduced by about $3 million.

timeline.title: Budget rebalancing approved
timeline.text: Reductions in every department cover $3.8 million in new labor costs. Nine Police Department positions that are not sworn officers are eliminated.

timeline.title: Mid-year report
timeline.text: The FY 2025/26 estimate stays balanced, with the Budget Uncertainty Reserve projected to end the year at $4.3 million.

timeline.title: 10 more Human Services positions
timeline.text: The City Manager writes that State and federal funding changes will require eliminating 10 more Human Services positions.

timeline.title: FY 2026/27 budget proposed
timeline.text: A $427.1 million budget with staffing and services at current-year levels and no capacity to restore earlier cuts.

timeline.title: FY 2026/27 budget adopted
timeline.text: The Council adopts the Operating Budget after hearings on June 2 and June 9.

timeline.title: Sales tax measure deferred
timeline.text: News reports say the Council voted unanimously to defer a half-cent sales tax measure estimated to raise $30 million to $35 million a year.
